record.title: Maximum weakly stable matchings in graphs without odd preference cycles
record.statement: Let (G,<) be a preference system with ties where in every odd cycle there is a node that prefers its clockwise neighbour to its other neighbour, and there is another node that prefers its anti-clockwise neighbour to its other neighbour. How well can we approximate the maximum size weakly stable matching?
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: Maximum weight bounded fractional matching
record.statement: Given a graph G=(V,E), and weight and capacity functions $w,u: E \to {\mathbb R_+}$ defined on the edge set, is there a combinatorial, strongly polynomial algorithm to find a vector x maximizing wx subject to the constraints $x \in P(G)$ and $x \leq u$, where P(G) is the convex hull of the incidence vectors of perfect matchings of G?
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: Maximum weight k-element subsets of perfect matchings
record.statement: Given a bipartite graph G with edge weights, can we find in polynomial time a maximum weight k-element matching in G that can be extended to a perfect matching?
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: Min-sum two edge-disjoint paths
record.statement: Let G=(V,E) be an undirected graph and let $(s_1,t_1), (s_2,t_2)$ be two node pairs. Give a combinatorial, polynomial-time algorithm to find edge-disjoint $s_1-t_1$ and $s_2-t_2$ paths with minimum total length.
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: Minimum k-way cut in a hypergraph
record.statement: Can we find a minimum k-way cut in a capacitated hypergraph in polynomial time, if k is fixed?
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: Orientation with shortest round trip
record.statement: Let G=(V,E) be a mixed graph with non-negative edge-lengths and let $s,t \in V$. Can we find in polynomial time an orientation where the sum of the lengths of the shortest s-t directed path and the shortest t-s directed path is minimal?
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: Parity constrained strongly connected orientations
record.statement: Find a good characterization for undirected graphs having a strongly connected (more generally k-edge-connected) orientation so that the in-degree of every node is odd.
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: S-T edge-connectivity augmentation
record.statement: Given a digraph D=(V,A), two (not necessarily disjoint) subsets $S,T\subseteq V$ and a connectivity requirement k, develop a strongly polynomial time combinatorial algorithm for finding a minimum cardinality arc-set whose addition makes D k-edge-connected between S and T, that is, it contains k edge-disjoint paths from any node in S to any node in T.
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: Sabidussi's compatibility conjecture
record.statement: Let G=(V,E) be an Eulerian graph with minimum degree at least 4, and let W be a closed Eulerian walk of G. Is it true that G has a cycle decomposition such that no pair of consecutive edges of W appear in the same cycle of the decomposition?
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: Strong colouring of matroid-graph pairs
record.statement: Let G=(V,E) be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta \geq 2$, and let M=(V,r) be a matroid that has $2 \Delta$ disjoint bases. Is it true that M has $2 \Delta$ disjoint bases that are all independent in G?
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: What is the minimum number of n-simplexes needed to triangulate the n-cube
record.statement: What is the minimum number of n-simplexes needed to triangulate the n-cube? See this.

record.title: Suppose G has n vertices and no induced copy of H
record.statement: Erdős, Hajnal: Suppose G has n vertices and no induced copy of H. Is there an ľ > 0, depending only on H, so that the homogeneous number of G (i.e., the size of the largest clique or independent set) is at least n^(ľ )? This is open even for a 5-cycle.

record.statement: Chung, Graham: Define the discrepancy of a graph to be the largest value of D(S,T) = | |S||T|/2 - e(S,T) |, over all disjoint vertex sets S and T. Suppose that G has no induced copy of some graph H. How large must the discrepancy be?
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Chung, Graham)

record.title: How many comparisons are needed to determine a linear order of the Boolean poset
record.statement: Fishburn, Pekec, Reeds: How many comparisons are needed to determine a linear order of the Boolean poset? That is, what is the fewest number of questions of the form "Is S < T?" must one ask in order to find out a linear ordering of all subsets of an n-set? Conjecture: n-1.
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Fishburn, Pekec, Reeds)

record.title: Show that the jump number of a random linear extension of a grid poset (i
record.statement: : Show that the jump number of a random linear extension of a grid poset (i.e., a product of chains) is close to the maximum w.h.p. (For the "symmetric grid" poset [m]^n, this is known for n = exp(o(log m)).)
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot)

record.title: ("Diamond-Free Posets Problem") What is the size of the largest subset of the Boolean lattice B_(n) which includes no B_
record.statement: Griggs, Lu: ("Diamond-Free Posets Problem") What is the size of the largest subset of the Boolean lattice B_(n) which includes no B_(2) as a subposet? (What is the maximum number of subsets of [n] so that there are no A, B, C, D with A < B, A < C, B < D, and C < D?)
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Griggs, Lu)

record.title: For any poset P, define ex(n,P) to be the size of the largest subset of the Boolean lattice B_(n) which includes no (inj
record.statement: Griggs, Lu: For any poset P, define ex(n,P) to be the size of the largest subset of the Boolean lattice B_(n) which includes no (injective) copy of P as a (not-necessarily induced) subposet. Show that lim_(n→∞) ex(n,P) n^(1/2) 2^( -n) exists.
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Griggs, Lu)

record.title: In the binary expansion of sqrt(2), are there arbitrarily long sequences of 0's
record.statement: Erdős: In the binary expansion of sqrt(2), are there arbitrarily long sequences of 0's? Can you find a single algebraic number with this property?
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Erdős)

record.title: Is it possible, for each positive integer n, to find positive integers a, b, and c so that 4/n = 1/a + 1/b + 1/c
record.statement: Erdős-Strauss : Is it possible, for each positive integer n, to find positive integers a, b, and c so that 4/n = 1/a + 1/b + 1/c ? See this.

record.title: A covering code of radius R is a set of binary n-words so that every binary n-word can be reached from one of the codewo
record.statement: A covering code of radius R is a set of binary n-words so that every binary n-word can be reached from one of the codewords by changing at most R bits. How big is the smallest covering code of radius R with n bits? It is known to be a constant c(R) times 2^(R )/ n^(R), but it's not known what c(R) is. Some believe that c(R) = R!.
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot)

record.title: An asymmetric covering code of radius R is a set of binary n-words so that every binary n-word can be reached from one o
record.statement: /Ellis/Kahng: An asymmetric covering code of radius R is a set of binary n-words so that every binary n-word can be reached from one of the codewords by changing at most R zeroes to ones. How big is the smallest asymmetric covering code of radius R with n bits? It is known to be a constant c(R) times 2^(R )/ n^(R), but it's not known what c(R) is. Some believe that c(R) = 2^(R) R!.
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Ellis/Kahng)

record.title: An asymmetric packing code of radius R is a set of binary n-words so that no binary n-word can be reached from more than
record.statement: /Ellis/Kahng: An asymmetric packing code of radius R is a set of binary n-words so that no binary n-word can be reached from more than one of the codewords by changing at most R zeroes to ones. How big is the largest asymmetric covering code of radius R with n bits?
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Ellis/Kahng)

record.title: A de Bruijn covering code of radius R is a binary string so that the set of words appearing as n consecutive symbols (wi
record.statement: Chung/: A de Bruijn covering code of radius R is a binary string so that the set of words appearing as n consecutive symbols (with wrap-around) is a covering code of radius R. What is the smallest de Bruijn covering code with parameters R and n? It is known to be between c2^(n)/n^(R) and c2^(n) log n/n^(R).
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Chung)

record.title: Is it true that, for some k, if all (K-1)-words are encountered by a t-ary word at the same rate as a uniform random t-a
record.statement: /Rorabaugh: Is it true that, for some k, if all (K-1)-words are encountered by a t-ary word at the same rate as a uniform random t-ary word, then this is also true for K-words, when K>k? That is, do substitution instance counts exhibit quasirandom threshold-like behavior?
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Rorabaugh)

record.title: Exact Dedekind numbers
record.statement: Let $M(n)$ be the number of monotone Boolean functions of $n$ variables, equivalently the number of antichains of subsets of an $n$-element set. Determine the exact values $M(n)$ for $n\geq10$.
record.source_name: Combinatorics problems from Wikipedia (proposed by Richard Dedekind)

record.title: Exact van der Waerden numbers
record.statement: Let $W(r,k)$ be the least $N$ such that every coloring of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with $r$ colors contains a monochromatic arithmetic progression of length $k$. Determine the unknown exact values of $W(r,k)$.
record.source_name: Combinatorics problems from Wikipedia (proposed by Bartel Leendert van der Waerden)

record.title: Classification of spherical quadrilaterals
record.statement: A spherical quadrilateral is a disk with four marked boundary vertices, curvature-one metric, geodesic sides, and interior angles $\pi\alpha_j>0$. Classify such quadrilaterals up to isometry: determine which angle quadruples with $\sum_j\alpha_j>2$ occur, which conformal moduli occur for prescribed angles, and when existence or uniqueness fails once angles larger than $\pi$ are allowed.
record.source_name: Eremenko - My favorite unsolved problems (proposed by Alexandre Eremenko and cited proposers)

record.title: Exceptional directions in Gross's theorem
record.statement: For a local inverse germ $\phi_z$ of a meromorphic function $f$ at a noncritical value $w=f(z)$, Gross's theorem gives analytic continuation along almost every ray from $w$. Sharpen 'almost every': what is the smallest possible exceptional set theorem, in capacity, dimension, or another natural sense?
record.source_name: Eremenko - My favorite unsolved problems (proposed by Alexandre Eremenko and cited proposers)

record.title: Goldberg's constant
record.statement: Let $f$ be holomorphic in the unit disk with exactly one simple zero $z_0$ and two $1$-points $z_1,z_2$, counted with multiplicity. Determine the largest universal lower bound $A_2$ for the radius of the smallest hyperbolic disk containing $z_0,z_1,z_2$, and determine whether an extremal function must have a double $1$-point.
record.source_name: Eremenko - My favorite unsolved problems (proposed by Alexandre Eremenko and cited proposers)

record.title: Two one-points in the unit disk
record.statement: Let $f$ be holomorphic in the unit disk, with $f(0)=0$, $f'(0)\ne0$, no other zeros, and exactly two solutions $z_1,z_2$ of $f(z)=1$, counted with multiplicity. Determine the minimum of $\max(|z_1|,|z_2|)$ and the maximum of $|f'(0)|$.
record.source_name: Eremenko - My favorite unsolved problems (proposed by Alexandre Eremenko and cited proposers)

record.title: Real two-one-point extremals
record.statement: Solve the two-one-point extremal problem for real holomorphic $f$: determine the minimum of $\max(|z_1|,|z_2|)$ and maximum of $|f'(0)|$ when $f(0)=0$, $0$ is its only zero, and $z_1,z_2$ are its two $1$-points.
record.source_name: Eremenko - My favorite unsolved problems (proposed by Alexandre Eremenko and cited proposers)

record.title: Belgian Chocolate constant
record.statement: Let $f$ be real and holomorphic in the unit disk, with one simple zero at $0$ and two simple $1$-points at $\pm ia$. Determine the minimum possible value of $a$.
record.source_name: Eremenko - My favorite unsolved problems (proposed by Alexandre Eremenko and cited proposers)

record.title: Rational Goldberg extremals
record.statement: For rational functions of each fixed degree, determine the analogues of Goldberg's constant and the unit-disk zero/one-point extremal quantities, and characterize their extremal functions.
record.source_name: Eremenko - My favorite unsolved problems (proposed by Alexandre Eremenko and cited proposers)

record.title: Maximum length of a polynomial lemniscate
record.statement: For a monic polynomial $p$ of degree $d$, determine the maximum length of the lemniscate $E(p)=\{z:|p(z)|=1\}$. Is the extremal asymptotically $p(z)=z^d+1$, giving maximum length $2d+o(1)$ as $d\to\infty$?
record.source_name: Eremenko - My favorite unsolved problems (proposed by Alexandre Eremenko and cited proposers)

record.title: Generic static-output stabilizability
record.statement: For real matrices $A\in\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times n}$, $B\in\operatorname{Mat}_{n\times p}$, and $C\in\operatorname{Mat}_{m\times n}$ with $n=mp$, determine for which pairs $(m,p)$ a generic system $\dot x=Ax+Bu$, $y=Cx$ admits a real static output feedback $u=Ky$ such that every eigenvalue of $A+BKC$ lies in the open left half-plane.
record.source_name: Eremenko - My favorite unsolved problems (proposed by Alexandre Eremenko and cited proposers)

record.title: Unfolding convex polytopes
record.statement: Does every three-dimensional convex polytope have a non-self-intersecting edge unfolding? Does a minimum spanning tree of the dual edge graph, with a natural dihedral-angle weighting, always specify such an unfolding? Does every convex polytope have a creased unfolding that cannot be refolded into a different convex polytope?
record.source_name: Erickson - Open Problems in Computational Geometry (proposed by Jeff Erickson and cited proposers)

record.title: Degenerate facets of polytopes
record.statement: A facet of a $d$-polytope is degenerate if it has more than $d$ vertices. Determine the maximum number of degenerate facets of an $n$-vertex $d$-polytope; in particular, can a four-polytope have at least $2n$ degenerate facets?
record.source_name: Erickson - Open Problems in Computational Geometry (proposed by Jeff Erickson and cited proposers)

record.title: Faces of intricate polytopes
record.statement: Determine the maximum total number of faces of a $d$-dimensional convex polytope with $n$ vertices and $n$ facets. In dimension four, do such fat-lattice polytopes have superlinear complexity? Are joins of polygons asymptotically optimal in dimensions at least six?
record.source_name: Erickson - Open Problems in Computational Geometry (proposed by Jeff Erickson and cited proposers)

record.title: Point-hyperplane incidences
record.statement: Given $n$ points and $m$ hyperplanes in $\mathbb R^d$ whose incidence graph contains no $K_{s,t}$, determine the maximum number of incidences. Of special interest is the case $n=m$ and $s=t=d$, where the known bounds are far apart.
record.source_name: Erickson - Open Problems in Computational Geometry (proposed by Jeff Erickson and cited proposers)

record.title: Halving lines and k-sets
record.statement: For an $n$-point planar set, determine the maximum number of halving lines. More generally, determine the maximum number of $k$-sets, subsets obtained by intersecting the point set with a half-plane, and extend the sharp bounds to higher-dimensional halving hyperplanes.
record.source_name: Erickson - Open Problems in Computational Geometry (proposed by Jeff Erickson and cited proposers)

record.title: Tangent pairs of pseudocircles
record.statement: For $n$ pseudocircles in general position, determine the maximum number of tangent pairs and the maximum number of digon cells. Determine whether the worst-case bounds for tangencies and digons are equal for genuine circles.
record.source_name: Erickson - Open Problems in Computational Geometry (proposed by Jeff Erickson and cited proposers)

record.title: Medial surfaces and Voronoi diagrams of lines
record.statement: Determine the worst-case complexity of the medial surface and of an offset surface of an $n$-feature polyhedron, and of the Voronoi diagram of $n$ lines in three-space. The known upper bounds are superquadratic while quadratic lower-bound constructions are known.
record.source_name: Erickson - Open Problems in Computational Geometry (proposed by Jeff Erickson and cited proposers)

record.title: Forced convex subsets
record.statement: Determine the exact Erdős–Szekeres number $f(n)$, the least number of planar points in general position forcing a convex $n$-gon. Also determine sharp bounds for empty convex polygons; the source's former empty-hexagon subproblem has since been resolved.
record.source_name: Erickson - Open Problems in Computational Geometry (proposed by Jeff Erickson and cited proposers)

record.title: Visibility complex of disjoint unit spheres
record.statement: Determine the combinatorial complexity of the visibility complex of $n$ pairwise disjoint unit spheres in three-dimensional space.
record.source_name: Erickson - Open Problems in Computational Geometry (proposed by Jeff Erickson and cited proposers)

record.title: Minimum-area triangles
record.statement: Given $n$ planar points, find a subquadratic algorithm for the minimum-area triangle or prove a quadratic lower bound in a suitable computation model. More generally, close the gap for minimum-volume simplices in fixed dimension.
record.source_name: Erickson - Open Problems in Computational Geometry (proposed by Jeff Erickson and cited proposers)

record.title: Complex collinearities
record.statement: Given $n$ points in $\mathbb C^2$, determine in quadratic time whether three lie on a complex line, or prove a quadratic lower bound; the known algorithm takes $O(n^2\log n)$ time.
record.source_name: Erickson - Open Problems in Computational Geometry (proposed by Jeff Erickson and cited proposers)

record.title: Extreme points
record.statement: For fixed $d>3$, determine whether every point of an $n$-point set in $\mathbb R^d$ is a convex-hull vertex faster than the best known near-$n^{2\lfloor d/2\rfloor/(\lfloor d/2\rfloor+1)}$ algorithm, or prove a matching lower bound.
record.source_name: Erickson - Open Problems in Computational Geometry (proposed by Jeff Erickson and cited proposers)
